title: Count Ways to Group Overlapping Ranges
summary: Given a 2D integer array ranges where each ranges[i] is defined as [starti, endi], split these ranges into two groups such that each range is assigned to exactly one group and no two overlapping ranges are placed in different groups.
statement: Given a 2D integer array ranges where each ranges[i] is defined as [starti, endi], split these ranges into two groups such that each range is assigned to exactly one group and no two overlapping ranges are placed in different groups. Calculate the total number of ways to split the ranges and return this number modulo 10^9 + 7.
constraints: Assign every closed interval to one of two labeled groups.
Any directly or transitively overlapping intervals must be in the same group.
Return the number of valid assignments modulo 1,000,000,007.
hints: Sort intervals by start and sweep while tracking the farthest end of the current overlap component.
A start beyond that farthest end begins a new independent component.
Each connected component must be assigned wholly to one group but has two labeled choices.
Components are independent, so c components produce 2^c valid assignments.
editorial: Components are independent, so c components produce 2^c valid assignments.

tests.explanation: The ranges overlap into one component, which may independently choose either group.
The first, third, and fourth ranges connect, while the second is separate, giving four assignments.
